origin.description: Removes every match by replacing each one with an empty string.

arguments.name: string
arguments.text: Input vector. Either a character vector, or something coercible to one.

arguments.name: pattern
arguments.text: Pattern to look for. A regular expression by default. fixed() compares literal text and coll() uses collation. A boundary, including the empty string, is an error.

origin.details: This is str_replace_all() with replacement "". Every match is deleted.
origin.value: A character vector the same length as string or pattern.
origin.example:
fruits <- c("one apple", "two pears", "three bananas")
writeLines(str_remove_all(fruits, "[aeiou]"))

translation.description: Removes every match by replacing each one with an empty string.

arguments.name: string
arguments.text: A string, or a list of strings and stringi._na.NA.

arguments.name: pattern
arguments.text: A string or list is an ICU regular expression. fixed, coll, and regex come from stringr.pattern.

translation.example:
from stringr.replace import str_remove_all
fruits = ["one apple", "two pears", "three bananas"]
for item in str_remove_all(fruits, "[aeiou]"):
    print(item)
